messages:
Maya (marketing): quick brain dump — want to align on a refreshed benchmark narrative for launch next week. goal: one slide that sells both latency and token-econ as linked benefits, and a short webinar pitch.
Ben (growth): love that. are we leaning into the ‘speed saves $’ angle or the ‘predictable latency for SLAs’ angle?
Maya (marketing): both — but different hooks by segment. SMB: speed = conversion + lower tokens. Enterprise: predictable tail latency + routing/fallback = reliability SLA.
Sara (creative): visual idea: a 2-panel chart — left = scatter of latency vs cost per 1k tokens (SMB use cases highlighted), right = timeline waterfall showing degraded tail vs our fallback. simple colors, no heavy text.
Leo (analytics): I can build the scatter with sample workloads. thinking of plotting median latency on x, token cost per 1k on y, sized by qps. want to show our quantized variants and hosted vs dedicated lines.
Priya (sales): routing + lead routing note: if we call out Enterprise SLA, we should include routing play in the webinar CTA — e.g., “request dedicated eval” that routes to AE. low-touch SMB CTA → self-serve checklist + 2-min demo.
Ben (growth): routing flow: inbound form has a tier selector, if selects Enterprise send to /sales/enterprise queue + nudges to book. If selects SMB, auto-nurture + product tour. we should mock copy for both.
Maya (marketing): agreed. Sara — can you draft two CTA lines? 1) Enterprise: “Request a dedicated evaluation — enterprise SLAs & private deployment.” 2) SMB: “Try our hosted API — speed and token savings, get free credits.”
Sara (creative): yep. I’ll make these microcopy options and 2 color variants. also proposing a 3-slide webinar flow: 1) Problem (latency + cost examples), 2) Benchmark (our charts + methods), 3) Customer paths + CTA routing.
Leo (analytics): quick note on methods for the bench slide — we should add a tiny footnote: workloads simulated with 128-token prompts, bursty QPS profile, quantization settings listed. analytics-bot: chart data prep job queued — job id: job_2026_03_21_88.
Maya (marketing): perfect. Leo — can you also export a CSV for Sara to generate charts? small fake sample is fine for mocks but we need the real CSV for the final deck.
Leo (analytics): will export. ETA 4 hours. I’ll include median/95p and token-cost calc per 1k tokens with taxonomy: hosted/dedicated/private and quantization flags.
Priya (sales): webinar logistics — we should reserve a private room for a sales-assisted demo after the webinar. AE on standby? @Priya volunteering to host the post-webinar enterprise office hours.
Ben (growth): webinar title candidate: “Speed & Spend: Reducing Latency and Token Costs for Real Apps” — feels a bit long. alternatives: “Speed that Pays” or “Faster + Cheaper LLMs.” thoughts?
Sara (creative): “Speed that Pays” is punchy. use that for social assets. the webinar title can be more descriptive: “Speed that Pays: Latency + Token-economics for Production LLMs.”
Maya (marketing): cool. next: landing page copy. short hero: “Predictable latency. Lower token costs. One API.” subhead: “Ship LLM features with consistent performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”
Ben (growth): landing funnel: inbound -> benchmark deck gated -> choose path (enterprise demo / self-serve credits). we should add an immediate microdownload (one-page cheat sheet) to reduce friction.
Priya (sales): microdownload = great. include a 1-page routing cheat for AEs; also capture upgrade intention flag in form (budget timeline).
Maya (marketing): action items: Leo — CSV + 95p numbers (4h). Sara — mock visuals + two CTA variants (EOD). Ben — landing funnel draft and form fields (tomorrow). Priya — AE office hours & routing play (tomorrow). I’ll draft webinar outline and email invite.
Sara (creative): small design Q — do we put sample customers on slide? could be risky. maybe use anonymized profiles: “ecommerce scale” / “enterprise search”.
Priya (sales): anonymized profiles is safer. please include one short quote mock from a PM that mentions latency improving conversion.
Maya (marketing): good call. one more: tag for tracking — utm=bench_speed_that_pays and a hidden field for lead_tier. Ben — can you add the tracking params to the landing draft?
Ben (growth): will do. also recommend A/B test on CTA wording for SMB: “Get free credits” vs “Try hosted API — free credits”.
Leo (analytics): will add A/B test metric hooks to the CSV so we can simulate signal.
analytics-bot: webinar calendar event created: 2026-03-30 16:00 UTC — event_id w-497123.
Maya (marketing): wrap up — this thread is our coordination channel for the bench narrative + routing. I’ll post the first draft in #marketing later today. :rocket: 
Ben (growth): thanks all — excited.
Sara (creative): working on assets now :paintbrush: 
Priya (sales): thanks — I’ll prep AE notes.
Leo (analytics): uploading CSV to /shared/marketing/bench/4971234567_bench.csv when ready.
